study_context.outcome: All-cause mortality at 28 days or in-hospital death
study_context.population: Trauma patients with significant bleeding or at risk of significant hemorrhage

Younger trauma patients (age < 40 years).hypothesis: Younger trauma patients (age < 40 years) benefit more from TXA because they have fewer comorbidities and higher likelihood of survival if hemorrhage is controlled early.

Trauma patients with initial systolic bl.hypothesis: Trauma patients with initial systolic blood pressure (isbp) < 90 mmHg will experience a greater reduction in 28-day all-cause mortality when treated with tranexamic acid compared with control.

subgroup_rule.description: Initial systolic blood pressure less than 90 mmHg (severe hypotension)

In trauma patients with an initial respi.hypothesis: In trauma patients with an initial respiratory rate of 20 breaths per minute or higher (irr >= 20), administration of tranexamic acid reduces all-cause 28-day or in-hospital mortality compared with no TXA.

subgroup_rule.description: Initial respiratory rate in breaths per minute; subgroup includes patients with tachypnea (>=20 bpm).

In trauma patients, those with icc >= 2.hypothesis: In trauma patients, those with icc >= 2 will have lower all-cause 28-day or in-hospital mortality when treated with tranexamic acid compared with controls.

subgroup_rule.description: icc value greater than or equal to 2

In trauma patients with an initial heart.hypothesis: In trauma patients with an initial heart rate of 120 beats per minute or higher, administration of tranexamic acid reduces 28-day or in-hospital all-cause mortality compared with no TXA.

subgroup_rule.description: initial heart rate (beats per minute) at or above 120
